properties.description: Pixel or sample dimensions, and aspect ratio.
Bits per channel, and the size of the representable colour set.
ICC profile or colour space; determines whether colours reproduce accurately.
Per-pixel transparency. Note the difference between a format supporting alpha and a file using it.
Temporal structure: duration, frame timing, animation, synchronisation.
Independently addressable planes or objects that have not been flattened together.
Whether text remains selectable, searchable and machine-readable, rather than becoming a picture of text.
Document hierarchy: headings, lists, tables, reading order.
Descriptive and embedded data: authorship, timestamps, EXIF, GPS, comments.
Embedded font programs, and whether glyphs render as the author intended.
Links, form fields, scripts, and other active behaviour.

Whether the sample values themselves survived, as distinct from how many there are or how wide each one is. This is the property lossy compression destroys. Measured with a domain metric — SSIM for raster, band energy or SNR for audio.
Channel count and layout, e.g. stereo or surround.
Audio samples per second.
Bits per audio sample.
Numeric precision of stored values, e.g. float versus integer.
Mesh connectivity: which vertices form which faces.
Surface appearance: textures, shaders, material assignments.
Skeleton, joints, weights and animation bindings.
Recorded history of the file's origin and prior processing.

measured.metric: band energy retained vs the WAV original, per octave band
measured.note:
THE EDGE THAT FORCED ADR-0014. Every property the vocabulary tracked came back
clean — channels 1 to 1, sample rate 44100 to 44100, duration unchanged — while
~10% of the signal energy was gone from the measured bands.

`bit_depth` could not express it, because MP3 has no fixed sample width and the
property does not apply at all; ffprobe reports bits_per_sample = 0. So the loss
had nowhere to be recorded. That is the same hole found in raster (§13.7), from
a different domain with a different metric, which is what justified adding
`signal_fidelity` to a closed vocabulary.

The FLAC edge below is the control: 100.0% retention on the same specimen
through the same harness. Without it, 90.3% could have been the measuring
instrument rather than the codec — a mistake this project has already made once
(§13.8).

REPRODUCIBLE SINCE 2026-08-25. This block previously cited "corpus/
generate_audio.py + ffprobe band-energy analysis". The generator is committed;
the analysis never was. The numbers were therefore unfalsifiable — and
CONTRIBUTING.md calls contradicting an entry with a measurement the most
valuable contribution anyone can make, which nobody could do here. The harness
now exists as tools/measure_audio.py, and re-running it reproduces the original
figures to four places: 0.9027 and 0.9026 against the recorded 0.903 and 0.902.
The old numbers were honest. They just could not be checked.

AND THEY WERE NOT REPRESENTATIVE. Both original specimens are pure sine tones,
the easiest case for a perceptual codec. Measuring across octave bands on
broadband and transient content shows the thing MP3 at 64k most conspicuously
does, which two tones could not reveal:

  band            highfreq        broadband   transient
  500-2000 Hz     0.9027          0.9054      0.9221
  8-16 kHz        0.9026          0.9869      0.9046
  16-22 kHz       n/a (absent)    0.0564      0.0003

**The top octave is deleted.** highfreq reads `n/a` there because a 1 kHz plus
15 kHz two-tone has no energy above 16 kHz at all — its 15 kHz component sits
inside the 8-16 kHz band. The specimen could not see the lowpass, so the
registry did not record it.

So `band_1khz_retained = 0.903` is true and remains true, and a consumer reading
it alone would conclude "MP3 at 64k costs about 10%". The honest summary is
"about 10% in the midrange, and everything above 16 kHz". Recorded here rather
than replaced, because the midrange figure is still the right answer to the
question it was asked.

The transient specimen also shows retention ABOVE 1.0 in the lowest bands (1.42
at 62-125 Hz): the codec ADDS energy where the original had little. That is
pre-echo, the classic MP3 artefact, and it is a reminder that a lossy codec is
not only subtractive. `signal_fidelity = degraded` covers it, but the direction
is worth knowing.

measured.metric: band energy retained vs the WAV original, plus SNR
measured.note:
Lossless, and serving as the control that makes the MP3 measurement above
credible.

STRENGTHENED 2026-08-25. This control previously rested on one number — 1.0
retention in the 15 kHz band of a two-tone specimen. It now runs on the
broadband and transient specimens as well, the same content that exposes MP3's
lowpass, and comes back **bit-identical**: 1.0000 in every octave band and an
infinite SNR.

That matters for what it rules out. The MP3 edge above reports 0.0564 retention
in the top octave, and the obvious suspicion about any such number is that the
harness invented it. If tools/measure_audio.py were fabricating loss on
hard content it would fabricate it here too, on the same specimens through the
same code path. It does not. The loss is the codec.

The specimen carries DIFFERENT tones in left and right (A4 and E5), because
downmixing identical channels is not observably lossy — the audio equivalent of
testing alpha with a fully opaque image (corpus/generate_audio.py).

`audio_channels` carries a `policy` of `downmix_average`, the audio analogue of
alpha's `composite_black` (ADR-0012): saying the channels are gone does not say
what replaced them, and averaging is one choice among several.

POLICY NOW MEASURED, 2026-08-25, where it was previously asserted. The left
channel's 440 Hz component comes back at **0.2500** of its original power —
half amplitude, exactly what averaging two channels predicts. The number
discriminates between the candidate policies rather than merely being
consistent with one: `take_first` would return 1.0, since the left channel
would pass through untouched.

`sox IN OUT remix 1,2` returns the same 0.2500 (registry/edges/sox.toml), so
both engines average and this edge's policy agrees with its neighbour's. The
earlier note said "whether other engines pick differently is UNMEASURED"; for
these two it now is measured, and they agree. That is a weaker claim than the
three-engine alpha result (§13.4) and should not be read as a general law —
two engines agreeing is how the alpha investigation started, before ImageMagick
turned out to differ.

`signal_fidelity = degraded` because a listener no longer hears what was in the
original stereo field, even though each sample is still full precision.

TRUNCATES where SoX rounds, introducing exactly half an LSB of DC offset — mean
output 127.5025 where offset-binary u8 centres on 128 (docs/RESEARCH.md §14.6).

On this specimen the signal peaks at 1.28 counts, so half a count is 39% of peak
and dominates the 3.8 dB SNR. On loud content the same offset is inaudible and
the two engines would look identical. The divergence is real and its visibility
is entirely a property of the specimen.

The `policy = "truncate"` qualifier here is the whole reason ADR-0012 exists:
this edge and the SoX one both report bit_depth = degraded, both correctly, and
one of them shifts your audio by half a count.

THE OUTLIER, CONFIRMED 2026-11-26. A third engine settled which behaviour is the
odd one out: GStreamer 1.24.2 with dither off writes samples byte-identical to
`sox -D` (registry/edges/gstreamer.toml). Two independent engines round; ffmpeg
truncates. The DC offset is now reproducible from the harness: `--dc` reports
-0.4975 steps of 8-bit, matching the figure first found with a one-off
histogram script.

measured.metric: SSIM (all planes) and PSNR vs the lossless reference
measured.note:
The control for the video edges, as FLAC is for audio: VP9's lossless mode
decodes BIT-EXACT to the FFV1 reference (SSIM 1.0, infinite PSNR) through the
same harness that scores the lossy edges below. A harness that invented loss
would invent it here too.

measured.metric: SSIM (all planes) and PSNR vs the lossless reference
measured.note:
Constant-quality VP9 (`-crf 40 -b:v 0`). Every frame kept, size and rate
unchanged; the loss is in the signal alone. ADR-0014 requires naming the
metric because video metrics disagree: both SSIM and PSNR are recorded.

measured.metric: SSIM (all planes) and PSNR vs the lossless reference
measured.note:
MPEG-4 Part 2 (the native `mpeg4` encoder, LGPL) at fixed quantiser 8.
Lower fidelity than VP9 above on both metrics, as a 1999 codec should be.

ERROR DIFFUSION, and the outlier again — three times the retained texture of the
other two engines and 67% more bytes. libvips was also the odd one out on alpha
flattening (ADR-0012), which is worth noting and not yet worth generalising from.

The SSIM here (0.9065) is LOWER than image-rs (0.9105) despite dithering being
generally preferred by human viewers. Fidelity scores cannot detect dithering —
all three engines land within 0.03 — so the policy is the only field that
distinguishes them. See §15.3.

255-COLOUR CAP, found 2026-11-26 on Govdocs1 (docs/RESEARCH.md §18.3).
libvips keeps at most 255 palette colours where GIF allows 256, so an image
with EXACTLY 256 colours, which fits a GIF palette with nothing lost, is
quantised anyway. On four real PNGs with exactly 256 colours the result had
203-238; image-rs and ImageMagick kept all 256. That is why the real_world
count below (15 of 39) exceeds the 11 real PNGs with more than 256 colours,
where every engine must reduce. Reproduce with corpus/raster/palette-256.png
(libvips gives 254); the test
`a_full_256_colour_palette_survives_image_rs_but_not_libvips_gifsave` pins it.

Nearest-palette, siding with image-rs against libvips two-to-one — the same
split as alpha flattening. Uses 252 colours where the others use 255; the
three-colour difference is unexplained and not worth chasing until it matters.

METADATA CORRECTED 2026-11-26, from `lost` to `degraded` (docs/RESEARCH.md
§18.5). ImageMagick carries a PNG's COMMENT text into the GIF's comment
extension and drops the rest. On the committed specimen
png-with-passengers.png, the comment "internal-doc-id-88213-do-not-share"
survives while `Author` does not; on 6 real Govdocs1 PNGs with metadata, the
comment survived in 4. libvips and image-rs carry neither. For anyone using
this conversion to strip a file before sharing it, that is the difference
that matters. Pinned by `imagemagick_carries_png_comments_into_gif`.

REAL-WORLD DEFECT, found 2026-11-26 on Govdocs1 (docs/RESEARCH.md §18.1). A PNG
carrying an `oFFs` page offset comes out as a GIF whose frame sits AT that
offset while the logical screen stays the image's own size, so the frame lies
outside the visible area. 2 of 39 real PNGs (303329, 189036); a negative offset
is clamped to 0 and is harmless. Decoders then disagree about the same file:

  image-rs     117x64, all black
  libvips      226x183, canvas enlarged to hold the frame
  ffmpeg       refuses: "Invalid top position: 119"
  ImageMagick  reads it back intact

libvips `gifsave` and image-rs write the frame at (0, 0). Reproduce with
`corpus/raster/png-with-offset.png`; the test
`imagemagick_moves_an_offset_png_outside_the_gif_screen` pins the behaviour.

No tracked property records this. `geometry` is resolution, which is
unchanged; the pixels survive; the loss is where they are placed. Noted here
rather than forced into a property that means something else.

edges.invocation: gst-launch-1.0 filesrc location=IN ! wavparse ! audioconvert ! audio/x-raw,format=U8 ! wavenc ! filesink location=OUT

measured.note:
Default `audioconvert` behaviour: TPDF dither, then ROUND to nearest. The output
stays centred on 128 (+0.0018 steps), where ffmpeg's sits half a step low.

5.12 dB sits beside SoX's dithered 5.09 to 5.16 dB. Unlike SoX the dither is
deterministic: three runs gave 5.12 dB each time, so this figure reproduces
exactly, where SoX's dithered figure moves in the second decimal place.

edges.invocation: gst-launch-1.0 filesrc location=IN ! wavparse ! audioconvert dithering=none ! audio/x-raw,format=U8 ! wavenc ! filesink location=OUT

measured.note:
THE TIE-BREAKER. With dither off, GStreamer's 8-bit samples are BYTE-IDENTICAL
to `sox -D`'s on the same specimen: same 11.11 dB, same +0.0014-step offset,
same histogram (129: 16,420 · 127: 16,360 · 128: 11,320).

So two independent engines round to nearest and one truncates. `truncate` is
ffmpeg's behaviour, not a convention, which is the same shape as the alpha
finding (§13.4): two engines agreeing and one differing, where only a third
engine could say which one was the outlier.

edges.invocation: gst-launch-1.0 filesrc location=IN ! wavparse ! audioconvert ! audio/x-raw,channels=1 ! wavenc ! filesink location=OUT

measured.note:
THIRD ENGINE, SAME ANSWER. The left channel's 440 Hz tone comes back at 0.2500
of its power, which is what averaging predicts, and the samples are
bit-identical to `ffmpeg -ac 1` (SoX already matched ffmpeg): run
`tools/measure_audio.py FFMPEG_MONO.wav GST_MONO.wav --snr` and it reports an
infinite SNR. Three independent
engines average, so `downmix_average` is a convention rather than a habit.

That answers the caution recorded on the ffmpeg downmix edge, that two engines
agreeing is how the alpha investigation started before a third one differed.
Here the third one agreed.

edges.invocation: gst-launch-1.0 filesrc location=IN ! wavparse ! audioconvert ! flacenc ! filesink location=OUT

measured.note:
Lossless, as FLAC must be. Recorded because it is the control for this engine:
the harness reads 1.0000 in every octave band through GStreamer's pipeline as
well as ffmpeg's, so the GStreamer measurements above are about the
conversions, not about the harness meeting a new decode path.

measured.alpha: lost on rgba-gradient; not exercised by the other three
measured.color_depth: degraded 16->8 on gray16; not exercised by the 8-bit specimens
measured.note:
Every measurement agrees with the declared vector, which is what earns the
`verified` status — CI rule 5 refuses it without this block.

Two results worth keeping. `rgba-opaque` is the control: it HAS an alpha channel
but every pixel is opaque, so dropping alpha is not an observable loss and the
harness reports `not-present-in-input` rather than `lost`. Distinguishing "the
format supports it" from "this file uses it" is what stops the harness
manufacturing agreement.

And gray16.jpg came out at 197.9% of its PNG input — the JPEG is LARGER. A
16-bit greyscale gradient is close to the best case for PNG's filters and close
to the worst case for JPEG's DCT. "Convert to JPEG to save space" is not a law
of nature, and the planner has no cost term that knows this yet.

Lossless in the only sense that applies: PNG re-encodes the already-decoded
JPEG pixels exactly, so SSIM against the JPEG it decoded is 1.0. It does NOT
recover what the original JPEG encode destroyed.

That distinction is exactly what the composition rules protect. On a
PNG -> JPEG -> PNG round trip the total still reports alpha as `lost`, because
`lost` is absorbing: arriving back at a format that supports transparency does
not bring the transparency back.

THE ARCHIVAL TARGET, and the only one that earns that description on evidence.
Across the four specimens TIFF is the ONLY target that preserved 16-bit depth:
gray16 came through with depth=preserved, while JPEG, GIF, BMP and WebP all
degraded it to 8-bit. Combined with SSIM 1.0 and intact alpha, this is the route
to pick when fidelity is the whole point.

The cost is size: 110,802 bytes for the specimen WebP stores in 218, also
losslessly. That is a genuine user-facing trade-off — archival fidelity versus
file size — and it is the first one in this registry backed by measurement
rather than intuition.

The most surprising measured result in the registry. image-rs writes LOSSLESS
WebP: SSIM 1.0000 on every specimen with alpha intact, at 218 bytes for the
image PNG needs 993 for and BMP needs 65,658 for. Roughly 4.5x smaller than PNG
and 300x smaller than BMP, with no measured loss.

`color_depth` is `degraded` rather than `preserved` because gray16 came back at
8-bit. So WebP is lossless in the SSIM sense while still narrowing depth — which
is precisely why loss is a vector and not a scalar (ADR-0004). A single quality
number would have to call this either "lossless" or "lossy" and both would
mislead.

Caveat kept deliberately: four synthetic specimens is not a finding. Widen the
corpus before treating WebP as the default lossless target.

The counterpart to JPEG, and the reason this registry can offer a real choice:
GIF and JPEG lose OPPOSITE things. JPEG keeps colour and discards transparency;
GIF keeps transparency and destroys colour.

`color_depth = "lost"` is forced by rule 4 — image/gif does not list
`color_depth` in `preserves`, because a 256-entry palette cannot carry source
colour depth at all. The measurement backs that up harshly: SSIM 0.7992 on
rgba-opaque and 0.8105 on the gradient, versus JPEG's 0.9950 on the same
specimens. This is the worst-scoring verified edge in the registry by a wide
margin, and it is CORRECT that it scores badly.

gray16 scores 1.0000 only because a 64x64 greyscale ramp has few enough distinct
values to survive palettisation — a reminder that a mean over four specimens
hides more than it shows.

Lossless and uncompressed. Loss-equivalent to WebP on every tracked property,
which makes it the test case for alternative DEDUPLICATION: two routes offering
the same trade-off are one choice, and the planner should not present both.

What distinguishes them is size, which the loss vector does not model:
65,658 bytes versus WebP's 218 for the same image. A planner that ranked on
fidelity alone would treat these as interchangeable. They are not. Recorded as
a known gap rather than quietly fixed with a fudge factor.

Return leg into the PNG pivot, so GIF can reach every other raster target
without its own edge to each. Lossless with respect to the GIF it decodes; it
does not recover the colours palettisation destroyed. Composition keeps that
visible: a PNG -> GIF -> PNG round trip still reports color_depth as lost,
because `lost` is absorbing.
Return leg into the PNG pivot. Preserves depth, so TIFF -> PNG -> TIFF is genuinely round-trippable at 16-bit.
Return leg into the PNG pivot.
Return leg into the PNG pivot.

Text survives: every word of the synthetic specimen, and a median 99.7% of
distinct words across 20 real Govdocs1 documents (catdoc as reference).

No real document kept a font it asked for: Arial and Times New Roman became
Liberation Sans and Serif (metric compatible), others DejaVu or Inter. See the
FONTS note at the top of this file before reading that as an engine property.

catdoc prints hidden table-of-contents bookmark ids (_Toc...), so `.doc`
number recall is not a precision measurement and is not recorded here.

A PDF of a spreadsheet keeps what was DISPLAYED, not what was stored.

precision: the specimen stores 25 values to full double precision and displays
two decimals; none of the stored values survives (0.0). On 16 real
spreadsheets with enough numbers to measure, a median 97.6% of distinct values
survive exactly, worst 25%: most real spreadsheets display what they store,
some do not. Inherent to printing a spreadsheet, not a LibreOffice defect.

text_as_text: a long text cell beside a filled one is CLIPPED at the
neighbour's edge. The specimen's glossary cell loses every word after
"Glossary: turb", and those are exactly its missing words (0.67 recall). The
same happens on real files: the worst, 490684.xls at 0.70, is a glossary cell.

Two real .xls files are Excel 4.0 worksheets (BIFF4, no OLE2 container) and
xls2csv reads nothing from them, so they are not in the real-file figures.

Slides survive; speaker notes do not, by default (they need the
ExportNotesPages filter option, which is a different invocation).

The real-file minimum, 300839.ppt at 0.77, is UNRESOLVED: the missing text is
in the raw file but in neither the slides, the notes, the hidden slides nor
LibreOffice's own model of the presentation. Possibly PowerPoint fast-save
residue, which a PDF should drop. Telling the cases apart needs PowerPoint.

catppt repeats slide text, which made the first word-recall figures read as
low as 0.11 on faithful PDFs; recall is over distinct words (§19).

CORRECTED 2026-08-21 (docs/RESEARCH.md §13.8, §13.9). An earlier version of this
block recorded a single `ssim_alpha = 0.4686` from a comparison that read stored
RGB and ignored alpha. That figure scored the comparison's own baseline, not the
engine.

For an alpha-LOSING conversion the score depends entirely on which background
the original is composited onto before comparing, and the ranking against
image-rs REVERSES between the two: 0.4010 against white, 0.9933 against black.
Neither is the engine's quality. Both are recorded, with the background named,
because a score without its background is not reproducible.

The finding that stands independent of any metric is the policy: this
invocation composites transparency onto BLACK, established by pixel arithmetic
(ADR-0012). `--background 255` composites onto white and is a separate edge
below (ADR-0013).

measured.depth_observed: gray16.png is ushort/grey16 in, uchar out
measured.note:
THE DEFAULT IS LOSSY, and badly so: SSIM 0.8362 on rgb-photo at 1,942 bytes.
image-rs writes the same pair LOSSLESS at SSIM 1.0 and 37,098 bytes. A consumer
reading "PNG to WebP" from the image-rs edge and then running libvips in their
own pipeline would silently get visibly degraded output.

`vips webpsave --lossless` is a separate edge, recorded below: 15,512 bytes at
SSIM 1.0, one flag apart from this one. See ADR-0013.

`color_depth` and `signal_fidelity` record two different things here, and the
distinction is the whole point of ADR-0014:
  - `color_depth = degraded {16 -> 8}` — WebP is 8-bit. Measured directly with
    vipsheader: gray16.png goes in as `ushort`/`grey16` and comes out `uchar`.
  - `signal_fidelity = degraded` — the lossy quantisation at SSIM 0.8362, which
    is not colour-depth loss at all and had nowhere to live before ADR-0014.

CORRECTED 2026-08-23. This edge previously claimed `color_depth = preserved`
while the `--lossless` edge below claimed `degraded {16 -> 8}` for the same
engine and the same format pair — WebP does not change bit depth based on a
compression flag, so both could not be right. The cause was that this edge's
specimen list omitted gray16.png, so 16-bit input was never exercised, and the
untested assumption was published as `verified`. gray16.png is now measured
here. Its note also still described `signal_fidelity` as "proposed and not yet
adopted" months after ADR-0014 adopted it, and described the `--lossless` edge
as missing after it had been added. Raised in review.
measured.tool: core/examples/libvips_edges.rs; vipsheader for the depth check

measured.note: Lossless on every specimen, alpha intact. Uncompressed by default and correspondingly large — 110,830 bytes for a 94,487-byte PNG.

measured.comparison_background: white (irrelevant here — alpha is preserved, so the score is 1.0 against any background)
measured.note:
Genuinely lossless, alpha included: SSIM 1.0000 on every 8-bit specimen. The one
exception is gray16 at 0.9997, which is not compression loss — WebP is 8-bit, so
16-bit input is truncated, and `color_depth` records that.

Contrast the DEFAULT invocation above, which is lossy at SSIM 0.8362 on the same
photo. Same engine, same formats, one flag apart, 15,512 bytes versus 1,942.
This pair is the clearest argument in the registry for ADR-0013.

This edge is also what exposed the measurement bug in RESEARCH.md §13.8: it
originally scored 0.4691 on rgba-hard-edge, which is impossible for a lossless
conversion and turned out to be the harness comparing premultiplied against
non-premultiplied stored RGB.

The same engine and formats as the default jpegsave edge, differing only by
`--background 255`, which composites transparency onto WHITE instead of black.

Scored against a white-composited original it reaches 0.9855 where the default
invocation reaches 0.4010. That is not evidence this invocation is better — it
is evidence that the comparison background and the flattening policy have to
agree, which is exactly why RESEARCH.md §13.9 says report the policy and never a
winner. Against a BLACK-composited original the ordering would reverse.

AGREES WITH FFMPEG EXACTLY. The two engines' mono output differs by 0.0% of
signal RMS on a specimen carrying different tones per channel — so both average
the channels, and `downmix_average` is a real convention rather than one
engine's habit.

Worth recording precisely because the alpha case went the other way (ADR-0012).
Cross-engine agreement is as much a finding as divergence, and is the easier one
to forget to write down.

DISAGREES WITH FFMPEG, and not only because of dither.

  ffmpeg default            3.8 dB
  ffmpeg -dither_method 0   3.8 dB   (flag had no visible effect)
  sox default               5.2 dB
  sox -D (dither disabled) 11.1 dB

Dither explains sox's own 5.9 dB spread — it trades SNR for the removal of
correlated distortion, which is the intended bargain. It does NOT explain the
7.3 dB gap between sox -D and ffmpeg. That cause is UNKNOWN and deliberately not
guessed at; see docs/RESEARCH.md §14.5.

The consequence for the schema is clear even though the cause is not:
`bit_depth = degraded` is under-specified in exactly the way `alpha = lost` was
before ADR-0012. It needs a policy vocabulary — `dither`, `truncate`, `round`
are the obvious candidates — and that vocabulary should not be written until
someone can explain the remaining gap, or it will encode a guess.

RESOLVED (this paragraph and the two above are kept as the record): the gap
was rounding versus truncation, §14.6, and `policy = "round"` now says so. A
third engine, GStreamer, rounds as well and with dither off produces samples
byte-identical to `sox -D` (§14.7). Re-measured 2026-11-26 with `--dc`: `sox -D`
reads +0.0014 steps, centred. The dithered SNR moves run to run (5.09 to 5.16 dB
across four runs) because SoX's dither is random; 5.09 is one run, not a
constant.

Specimen note: measured on QUIET content, where 8-bit quantisation is
catastrophic. The same conversion on loud content scores around 50 dB and the
engines would look identical. A property is only measurable on a specimen that
exercises it.
